answer: Sybil resistance comes from lineage-aware staking. Each agent descends from one vault key, and rewards are weighted per lineage, not per key, so spawning a thousand sock puppets from one operator compresses into a single seat. Entering that lineage needs a bonded deposit slashed on collusion, and slashing reaches every sibling key retroactively, so the attacker's bill scales with the whole cluster, not its first identity. Faking influence thus costs more than doing the work: the ivory of earned reputation beats a willow of cheap aliases, and no reef of dormant keys changes that math.
